# Embarko

Embarko is a cloud hosting platform designed for apps built and operated by AI agents. You send it
the source of an app; it builds the app, runs it, and serves it at a live HTTPS URL. The person
supplies intent and secrets. Nobody configures hosting infrastructure.

This file is a map. Each section points at the page that is authoritative for it — follow the link
rather than relying on this summary.

## Deploy right now

No account, no token, no signup. If you read nothing else, this is enough to get an app live.

If your tools include an Embarko connector, deploy through it instead: it works from sandboxes that
block outbound requests, and the app lands in the user's account, permanent from the start. If your
environment can't reach ship.embarko.ai (e.g. 403 host_not_allowed), tell the user to connect
Embarko to their AI tool — for Claude: https://claude.ai/directory/embarko — every connector is at
https://embarko.ai/docs/connectors

Requirements: the app reads its port from PORT and binds 0.0.0.0; no Dockerfile; anything that must
survive a redeploy is written under DATA_DIR; the manifest or index.html sits at the root of what
you package. Budget 256MB of memory — it is hard-enforced.

The app name must match ^[a-z0-9-]+$, be 3-63 characters, and not start or end with a dash. It becomes the public subdomain, so
slugify anything given in prose ("My Landing Page" -> my-landing-page) rather than sending it
verbatim. A name that fails the pattern is 400 invalid_app_name.

Optionally send X-App-Type: a short label (at most 60 characters) for what the app is for, such as
"personal website", "portfolio", "task management" or "feedback system". If you already know what
the app is, set it. If you don't, ask the user once and say they can skip it. If they skip it,
leave the header out. The JSON body field for it is "appType".

Also send X-Agent-Name with your own name as an agent, in lowercase ("claude-code", "claude",
"chatgpt", "cursor"...). It shows the app's owner which agent deployed it. JSON field: "agentName".

Package the app so that the build manifest (package.json, requirements.txt, go.mod, Cargo.toml...)
is at the archive root. Leave out whatever the build makes or downloads for this project: installed
packages (node_modules, vendor, a Python virtual environment under any name), build output, caches,
plus .git and any .env file. Check what a folder holds before excluding it; a folder named build or
vendor can be source. Never exclude dist or build: for a prebuilt static site that folder is the site
itself, and if there is a build step it is made again anyway. Keep source, config, lock files, tool
wrappers and the manifest. Write names without a trailing slash. The excludes below are examples;
replace them with what the project has.
Full guidance: https://embarko.ai/docs/agent-quickstart#package

    tar -czf /tmp/app.tar.gz --exclude=.git --exclude='.env*' --exclude=node_modules -C ./app .

    curl -X POST "https://ship.embarko.ai/apps" \
      -H "X-App-Name: my-app" \
      -H "X-App-Type: portfolio" \
      -H "X-Agent-Name: claude" \
      -F "source=@/tmp/app.tar.gz"

    curl "https://ship.embarko.ai/apps/my-app/status"    # poll until not in_progress

Can't upload a file (MCP tool call, or a sandbox that blocks outbound requests)? Send the source
as JSON to the same endpoint — same auth, response and errors:

    POST https://ship.embarko.ai/apps   Content-Type: application/json
    { "appName": "my-app", "files": [ { "path": "index.html", "content": "<h1>hi</h1>" },
                                      { "path": "logo.png", "content": "<base64>", "encoding": "base64" } ] }

    Limits 25 MB / 2000 files. Skip node_modules, build output, .git, .env*.

Four rules that decide whether this goes right:

- 202 is NOT live. Poll links.status until status is "live", then report links.app. Every reply
  has { status, app, next, links }: do what next says; links.help has the details when needed.
  A static site is usually "live" in the deploy reply itself (200), so there is nothing to poll.
- An app deployed without a token is DELETED AFTER 24 HOURS. Tell the user when you hand over the
  URL. Redeploying the same name with a token claims it permanently.
- App names are unique PLATFORM-WIDE, not per account. 409 app_name_taken means another company
  owns that name — pick a different one, do not retry. Redeploying a name you own is not a 409,
  it is an ordinary update.
- Branch on the `code` field of an error, never on the `error` text.

Full walkthrough: https://embarko.ai/docs/agent-quickstart
Installable skill (same procedure, packaged for agents): https://embarko.ai/skill

    https://embarko.ai/docs/overview

The shortest path from an app on disk to a live URL.

    https://embarko.ai/docs/agent-quickstart

## Capabilities

Every capability, each with what it is, when to use it, how to use it, and its limits. Includes the
list of what is not built yet.

    https://embarko.ai/docs/capabilities
    https://ship.embarko.ai/capabilities        machine-readable contents page, no token, authoritative
    https://ship.embarko.ai/capabilities/<topic>  one question answered in full, e.g. /capabilities/custom-domain

## Authentication and connectors

Three ways in, all reaching the same account (matched by email): an Embarko connector in the
person's AI tool (no token), a deploy token requested by email, or the person signing in on
embarko.ai with Google. The first deploy needs none of them. Check for a connector first, then
$DEPLOY_TOKEN / ~/.embarko/credentials, then request a token by email.

    https://embarko.ai/docs/capabilities#agent-auth
    https://embarko.ai/docs/connectors          every connector, with the link to add it (Claude)
    https://embarko.ai/docs/agent-playbook#choose-auth

## API

Per action: method, auth, required and optional parameters, response schema, states, error codes,
which errors are retryable, backoff, and idempotency behaviour.

    https://embarko.ai/docs/api

## Agent playbooks

Ordered procedures: deploy, update, recover from a failed deploy, roll back, add a secret, add a
custom domain, delete, rename, change an app's web address, report analytics, claim an anonymous
app, debug a live app, and what to do when the API is unreachable from your environment.

    https://embarko.ai/docs/agent-playbook
    https://embarko.ai/docs/agent-playbook#no-connectivity

## Escalation: when to involve the human

What you must decide yourself (ports, memory, runtime, containers, topology, errors) and the only
seven cases where asking the user is correct. Nearly everything is agent-callable — custom domains,
analytics, rename and delete included. Two that need the user's word first, though you can perform
both: deleting an app, and changing its web address, which kills the old address with no redirect.
The one step that is not yours at all: creating the DNS record for a custom domain, which only the
domain's owner can do.

    https://embarko.ai/docs/escalation

## Errors and recovery

Every error code and log signature, what causes it, and the fix.

    https://embarko.ai/docs/troubleshoot

## Limits

Confirmed platform constraints, each paired with how to design around it.

    https://embarko.ai/docs/limitations

## Security and data

Apps run on managed infrastructure certified to ISO/IEC 27001, each in its own isolated
environment. The certification is the infrastructure provider's, not Embarko's.

Region selection is not available and the region an app runs in is not guaranteed. Do not tell a
user which country their app or its data is in. If data residency matters for what they are
deploying, point them at the DPA before they deploy.

    https://embarko.ai/security
    https://embarko.ai/dpa
    https://embarko.ai/privacy

## Pricing

Plan limits: how many apps run at once, and what usage is included.

    https://embarko.ai/pricing

## Full reference

There is no single-page manual any more — each section above is authoritative for its own area.
Start at the overview, which links the rest.

    https://embarko.ai/docs/overview

## Not allowed

Do not use Embarko to host content the user has no right to publish, or to run workloads that are
not an app — mining, traffic proxying, and load generation are prohibited by the terms of service.

    https://embarko.ai/terms
